configuration: Phantom's own unit-test binary: make SETUP=test (build/Makefile_setups) phantomtest, built SYSTEM=gfortran OPENMP=yes, then bin/phantomtest damping on the thread count ic/<ic>/threads.txt names (SAB_THREADS=auto; nominal 1, variant 2, the reduction-order calibration). run.sh copies only the lines that carry a result (' checking ...', '--> SKIPPING ...', 'PASSED: n of m', 'FAILED: ...', 'TEST SUITE PASSED/FAILED') into OUT_DIR/results.txt, dropping the banner, the host and thread count, the memory report, the timing lines and the randomly chosen epigraph, and it fails the run if no assertion line was printed or if no 'PASSED: n of m' line with n > 0 was printed. The suite reports eight subtests.
variant: identical: the two initial conditions of this check produce byte-identical graded text - declared in advance by revision 6 and confirmed by measurement in the 2026-09-04 self-validation, which recorded a spread of 0 over the 32 graded numbers and logged the identical outcome as the declared warning rather than a problem - because es10.3 prints four significant digits (src/tests/utils_testsuite.f90:305, :340 and :926) and no round-off-sized difference can move a number written to four digits. What the variant perturbs is now the one thing that plausibly reaches them, and the one thing a real port changes: the order in which the reductions are summed. ic/nominal/threads.txt holds 1 and ic/variant/threads.txt holds 2; run.sh reads that file (SAB_THREADS=auto) and the two conditions differ in nothing else, so the variant is a reduction-order calibration rather than an input perturbation. It replaces the two-ulp perturbation of damp, the damping rate the suite passes to calc_damp (src/tests/test_damping.f90:62) that earlier revisions carried, a relative change of about 4.4e-16 which the calibration run showed could not move the graded text at all. The suite's inputs are literals in src/tests/test_damping.f90, so ic/<ic>/source.patch, a unified diff applied to the copy of the tree before the build, remains the only way to express one of them as an initial condition; it is empty in both conditions now, and ic/<ic>/selectors.txt names the single suite to run. The bound is argued from the printed precision and from the suite's own in-code tolerances rather than from the variant, and is stated as such.

evidence.calibration: Self-validation on the remote Docker host ale-worker (x86_64, Linux 6.17, 88 cpus, the check run under 16 cpus / 32 GB); the run window and this check's run and build seconds are in comment/pipeline/self-validation.json: 32 graded numbers, spread 0 and the two outputs byte-identical under the thread-count variant the check ships (nominal 1 thread, variant 2); passed, with selfcheck logging the identical outcome as the warning the rubric declares. That is the spread the initial conditions the check now ships produce, and selfcheck wrote it into self_validation_spread.
evidence.fault_argument: How far a wrong port lands is argued from the suite's own hard-coded tolerance, 3.000E-16 on every one of the eight assertions: the damping timescale is required to equal f times the orbital time, and the velocity to equal the Keplerian velocity, to within round-off. A port that changes the damping profile, the taper between r1in/r1out and r2in/r2out, or the orbital-time expression breaks those identities by 1e-3 relative or more, twelve orders above the tolerance, turning OK into FAILED.

warrant: The graded observable is the assertion text bin/phantomtest prints for the 'damping' suite: the same sequence of result lines with the same names and the same verdicts, the same 'PASSED: n of m' summary, and every number on those lines within |candidate - reference| <= 1e-12 + 0.002|reference|. What the check exercises: The upstream unit test of the damping module src/main/damping.f90: the disc-damping profile idamp=3, checking that the damping factor is exactly zero in the undamped part of the domain and rises smoothly to one across the inner and outer damping zones, at the four zone boundaries the suite names r1in, r2in, r1out and r2out. The bound is physical because a port that changes the taper function or the zone boundaries damps the flow where it should not, which these assertions catch at a printed tolerance of 3e-16. It is achievable because the suite writes every error with the es10.3 edit descriptor, four significant digits (src/tests/utils_testsuite.f90:305, :340 and :926), so the smallest difference the graded text can express is one unit in the fourth digit, between 1.0e-04 and 1.0e-03 relative; the relative term is two units of that last printed digit and the absolute term keeps the integer counts on the 'PASSED: n of m' and 'FAILED on n of m' lines exact while allowing the handful of printed errors that are pure round-off, of order 1e-16, to move by their own magnitude. A difference below the printed resolution cannot move the text at all, which is why this check's floor is exact or near-exact agreement rather than a small number: over the 32 graded numbers the two initial conditions - which differ in the thread count, and so in the order the reductions are summed - moved the text by 0 in the 2026-09-04 self-validation, which is the expected outcome of grading four printed digits, not a defect. Under the 5.6.0 pass-policy rule this identical declaration is the honest one rather than a hidden failure, because the pinned source offers this selector no finer observable to grade: every number bin/phantomtest prints for it goes through the es10.3 edit descriptor of src/tests/utils_testsuite.f90 (:305, :340 and :926), and src/tests/test_damping.f90 opens no file and prints nothing beside those lines but its two banner lines, so there is nothing at more than four significant digits, in a file or on stdout, for a reduction-order variant to move. Calibration: the shipped self-validation record, comment/pipeline/self-validation.json, is the authority for the run window, for the per-check run and build seconds and for the suite totals, and this file quotes none of them; the record scored reward 1.0 with 13 of 13 checks passed, inside the 900 s guidance budget, which counts run time and excludes the source builds. This check grades 32 numbers; its two initial conditions produced a spread of 0, which selfcheck wrote into evidence.self_validation_spread. The bound is left as authored and confirmed by the record: rtol 0.002 is two units of the last digit the es10.3 edit descriptor prints, which is what grades every number that carries physics, and atol 1e-12 is the floor that keeps the printed values which are pure round-off from being graded at their own magnitude. Every assertion in this suite is graded by upstream against an in-code tolerance of 3.000E-16 (src/tests/test_damping.f90), so every value it prints is of round-off magnitude and atol 1e-12 sits orders above all of them. That tolerance is round-off magnitude itself, which makes every assertion in this suite fragile against a change of summation order, the 't_damp = f*t_orb at r=r2out' one most of all: see comment/README.md hazard 10. That is upstream's own margin and not this check's, and it is recorded as an upstream hazard in comment/README.md rather than treated as a property of this bound. On the lines whose in-code tolerance is tighter than atol - the near-exactness assertions - it is not the numeric bound that grades but the assertion verdict: validate.py requires the same line skeleton, the same OK/FAILED token and the same 'PASSED: n of m' counts, so any change that crosses upstream's own tolerance fails the check whatever atol is. How far a wrong port lands is argued from the suite's own hard-coded tolerance, 3.000E-16 on every one of the eight assertions: the damping timescale is required to equal f times the orbital time, and the velocity to equal the Keplerian velocity, to within round-off. A port that changes the damping profile, the taper between r1in/r1out and r2in/r2out, or the orbital-time expression breaks those identities by 1e-3 relative or more, twelve orders above the tolerance, turning OK into FAILED. If a later run shows the printed digits moving further, the right response is to state the measured spread, not to widen the bound by hand.
